summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Parturition is a complex neuroendocrine reflex initiated by the fully developed fetus and placenta, producing the Fetal Ejection Reflex (Ferguson Reflex), driving maternal posterior pituitary Oxytocin release in a self-amplifying positive feedback loop. Lactation: Prolactin (anterior pituitary, milk synthesis in alveoli) vs Oxytocin (posterior pituitary, milk let-down / ejection via myoepithelial contraction). Colostrum provides rich maternal Secretory IgA antibodies.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 10.1 Neuroendocrine Mechanism of Parturition

Parturition (childbirth) is the expulsion of the mature fetus from the uterus at the end of gestation (average duration $\approx 280\text{ days}$ or $40\text{ weeks}$ from the first day of the last menstrual period, LMP).

1. **Initiation**: Signals for parturition originate from the **fully developed fetus and placenta**, which induce mild uterine contractions called the **Fetal Ejection Reflex**.
2. **The Ferguson Reflex**: Mechanical stretching of the cervix by the descending fetal presenting part activates baroreceptors, sending sensory neural impulses up the spinal cord to the maternal hypothalamus.
3. **Oxytocin Positive Feedback Loop**: In response, the maternal posterior pituitary neurohypophysis discharges **Oxytocin**. Oxytocin binds myometrial G-protein coupled receptors, generating vigorous contractions. Each contraction drives the fetus deeper into the cervix, increasing cervical stretch, firing more neural signals, and releasing even higher surges of oxytocin in a self-amplifying positive feedback cycle until delivery occurs.

### 10.2 Lactation Physiology & Colostrum

```
                         HORMONAL CONTROL OF LACTATION
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
   PROLACTIN (PRL)                                            OXYTOCIN
   ├── Anterior Pituitary Hormone                             ├── Posterior Pituitary Hormone
   ├── Stimulates **Milk Synthesis & Secretion**              ├── Stimulates **Milk Ejection / Let-Down Reflex**
   └── Acts on Mammary Alveolar Epithelial Cells              └── Contracts Mammary **Myoepithelial Cells**
```

- **Suckling Reflex**: Infant suckling on the nipple sends tactile neural signals to the maternal hypothalamus, simultaneously suppressing Dopamine (Prolactin Inhibiting Hormone, PIH) to release Prolactin, and firing supraoptic/paraventricular nuclei to discharge Oxytocin.
- **Colostrum**: The yellowish, viscous milk secreted during the first $2\text{--}3\text{ days}$ postpartum. It is low in fat and high in proteins, minerals, and rich in **Secretory $\text{IgA}$ Antibodies (sIgA)**, which coat the infant's gut mucosa to provide passive mucosal immunity against gastrointestinal and respiratory infections.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Cervical Ripening with Prostaglandins
conceptBreakdown.title: Cervical Ripening with Prostaglandins
conceptBreakdown.content: Prior to labor contractions, fetal cortisol and maternal estrogens induce endometrial production of Prostaglandins (PGE2, PGF2alpha) that degrade collagen fibers to soften and efface the cervix (cervical ripening).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Lactational Amenorrhea
conceptBreakdown.title: Lactational Amenorrhea
conceptBreakdown.content: Intense, frequent infant suckling maintains high systemic prolactin levels, which suppress hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility and pituitary LH/FSH secretion, preventing follicular maturation and ovulation during exclusive breastfeeding for up to 6 months.
